evidence_items.publisher: Nye, Tessler, Tenenbaum and Lake; arXiv / NeurIPS
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, final sentence; full paper sections 3–6
evidence_items.explanation: Adding a symbolic world model and consistency checks improves performance, supporting the proposed mechanism in limited domains. The intervention also adds reasoning and search, so it does not isolate absent cognitive models as the general cause of language-model failures.

evidence_items.publisher: Li, Nye and Andreas; ACL 2021, ar5iv rendering
evidence_items.locator: Section 6, Conclusion, first sentence; section 5, Limitations
evidence_items.explanation: Experiments on BART and T5 challenge an absolute absence of internal situation representations. The authors nevertheless leave open whether prediction errors arise from representation errors and whether the findings extend to richer worlds, so this does not refute the contextual robustness claim.

Later experiments connect legal move generation with inferred causal structure in game-trained GPT models. These are different systems and tasks, and the reported association does not establish Marcus's broad causal diagnosis.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed experiments do not establish that representation deficiencies are a central cause across the relevant language models and tasks.
Adding a world model also adds information, computation, reasoning, or search; the reviewed evidence does not fully separate those effects.
Simple learned representations and failures of robust reasoning can coexist. Neither establishes the broad claim by itself.
